discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany (EPTA)

nominees.name: Richard N. Manchester
nominees.affiliation: CSIRO Space and Astronomy, Australia (Parkes Pulsar Timing Array)

motivation: By timing ensembles of millisecond pulsars to ~100-nanosecond precision over decades, pulsar timing arrays turned the Galaxy into a gravitational-wave detector sensitive to light-year wavelengths. In 2023 NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA jointly reported a common red-noise process with the Hellings-Downs angular correlation, the defining quadrupolar signature of gravitational waves, opening the nanohertz band, which is most plausibly populated by supermassive black-hole binaries. McLaughlin co-founded and led NANOGrav, building its timing programme and instrumentation. Kramer led European precision timing, the Large European Array for Pulsars and MeerKAT timing, and pioneered strong-field gravity tests with the Double Pulsar. Manchester founded the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array and the International PTA framework that made the global combination possible. Their sustained efforts in instrumentation, timing methodology and collaboration opened an entirely new window on the gravitational-wave universe, complementary to LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA.
